target_customer: Operations teams at warehouses, 3PLs, distributors and retailers buying indirect supplies
problem: Indirect purchases are scattered across vendors with poor spend control and manual ordering.
business_model: Procurement platform (SaaS and marketplace); pricing not found

founders.name: Kais Baillargeon
founders.background_notes: Operations roles in the Middle East per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Catalog, order and approval workflows; later email to ERP order automation.

defensibility.rationale: Vendor catalogs and approval workflows create some lock in but procurement software is widely copied.

market_need_then: Indirect spend is fragmented and hard to control; the company cites 12 to 15 percent savings and 92 percent faster ordering claims (own site, unverified).

identity.logo: Wordmark with blue accent and dark navy

brand_strength.rationale: Very generic name shared by many companies and the domain needs a try prefix; no brand press found.

pivots.from: Marketplace to shop millions of products from vendors in one place (YC page)
pivots.to: Indirect procurement and spend management platform with AI agent
pivots.why: Not stated; seed announcement positions it around everyday spend (2025).

outcome_analysis: Response began in the S20 batch as an inventory marketplace and has become an indirect procurement platform with an AI ordering agent. It raised a 4 million seed only in January 2025, nearly five years after YC, so progress was slow, and the generic name and tryresponse domain cost it some searchability. It remains active and small.
notes: Seed amount 4.16M per Seedtable and 4M per the press release (4.3M total to date); press release used. Cornell news 2020 says Response worked with hundreds of procurement officers in over 40 countries (not opened beyond snippet). Faire and Grainger appeared in searches but no source names them as Response rivals, so the competitor list is empty. Brand effect 'hurt' is a judgment from name collisions, weakly sourced; one aggregator says one employee versus 11 to 50.
